decisions.reason: Adding 5V-rail current monitoring does not change the DCDC1 voltage, rating, or role on the 3.3V rail.
The client explicitly identifies the LEDs, together with the SPS30 and ZE08, as consumers of the 5V rail, extending the boost rail's current powered-load list.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: regarding power metering: I need to measure the 5V rail current as well — the SPS30, ZE08 and LEDs are the heaviest consumers so it's actually more important than the 3.3V rail. The only way I knew how to do it was adding a second INA219 at address 0x41, but wanted to ask if you have a better idea?

decisions.reason: Monitoring an additional rail does not change the AXP2101 battery input, normal-operation source, or system-load coverage.
The 5V current-monitoring decision does not affect the battery NTC connector or thermal-protection behavior.
The source does not change battery overcharge, overdischarge, short-circuit, or protection-component requirements.
The added 5V-rail measurement has no entailed effect on the battery connector family, pins, part number, or unresolved pin order.
The reference to heavy LED consumption does not change the charge-status display or dedicated charge-LED interface.
The standalone USB supply remains limited to the 3.3V rail; measuring 5V current does not alter its regulator, activation, or source-selection behavior.
The addressable LEDs are already specified as powered from the 5V rail, and current monitoring does not change their supply, switching, or level-shifting requirements.
The source does not establish any change to interboard power pins, signal pins, connector types, or pin-order policy.
The additional rail-monitoring requirement does not change the selected ESP32-S3 module or its part number.
The 5V current-monitoring decision does not affect USB data lines, enumeration, or the programming-port role.
